ApprovalDecideParams.description:
`approval/decide` params (tdd SS5.4): the decision. A standard SS3
command — requires the session loaded on this host, requires `commandId`,
durable intake before ack, value-identical replay.

feedback.description:
Free-text guidance delivered to the model with the denial. Only valid
on choices with `acceptsFeedback`. Never persisted in the durable
audit record (live steer only), so it is absent from
`approval/resolved` (tdd SS5.4). Omitted and explicit `null` both
mean "no feedback" (#23468).

requirementId.description:
Must equal the approval's `currentRequirementId`. The multi-stage race
guard: a decision aimed at stage 1 can never accidentally satisfy
stage 2, and a stale value is -32053 (tdd SS5.4).

ApprovalDecideResult.description:
`approval/decide` result (tdd SS5.4). Admission-ack rules still apply: the
authoritative outcome is `approval/resolved` / `approval/updated` on the
view stream.

approvalId.description: The approval this decision was applied to.

terminal.description:
`false` when the choice satisfied a stage but further requirements
remain (the approval stays pending and an updated `approval/request`
follows); `true` when this decision produced the terminal
`DecisionApplied` (tdd SS5.4).

ApprovalListPendingParams.description:
`approval/listPending` params (tdd SS5.7): the pull dual of the re-issued
requests. A log-fold read — no lease, works on loaded and unloaded
sessions, never subscribes.

ApprovalListPendingResult.description:
`approval/listPending` result (tdd SS5.7). Ordering is by opening
`viewCursor`; empty arrays when nothing is pending. The result is
point-in-time — to act on it race-safely, `approval/decide` carries the
`requirementId` guard regardless of how the client learned the state.

approvals.description:
Exactly the `approval/request` params of tdd SS5.3, one per pending
approval.

userInputs.description:
Exactly the `userInput/request` params of tdd SS5.10, one per pending
prompt.

ApprovalMode.description:
The approval enforcement modes (tdd SS5.12, camelCased
`ApprovalBackendMode`). **Closed** by design (D-006, select-never-create):
a client selects a preconfigured mode and can never construct one;
widening this enum is a deliberate, gate-visible protocol change.

ApprovalModeApplyOutcome.description:
Whether a mode change did anything (tdd SS5.12), mirroring
`ApprovalReconfigureApplyOutcome`. Apply failures are `commandRejected`.

ApprovalModeSource.description:
How an approval mode took effect (tdd SS5.12, the effective-mode
projection's `source` vocabulary). Open.

ApprovalRequirementRef.description: Approval-stage token carried in SS5 params and stale-requirement errors.

ApprovalResolutionSummary.description: Winning terminal returned to a losing `approval/decide` command.

ApprovalResolvedParams.description: `approval/resolved` params: the first durable terminal decision.

ApprovalSubject.description:
Open approval subject union. Unknown kinds are rendered generically and
never auto-approved by clients (tdd SS5.2).

kind.description: Open discriminator: `shell | fileAccess | network | process | tool`.

ApprovalUpdatedParams.description: `approval/updated` params: the refreshed pending view plus one change.

BackgroundInitiator.description:
Who durably backgrounded a task (tdd SS4.5.5,
`TaskBackgroundedInitiator`). Open — runtime vocabulary.

BranchState.description: The latest branch observation in the snapshot (tdd SS4.6.4, SS4.9.1).

branch.description: The observed branch; `null` on a detached-HEAD observation.

vcs.description: The detected version-control system; absent when none was detected.

CapabilityName.description:
A grantable capability name (SS1.4.4). Open: the reserved `rawLog` entry
joins this domain as an additive open-enum extension when SS6 un-defers
(#13929, Scenario 5 AS-3) — closed would make that a retype.

ClientCapabilities.description:
The client's requested capability posture (SS1.4.1). Every member
defaults; an absent `capabilities` object means all defaults.

experimentalApi.description: Opt into experimental methods, fields, and variants (default `false`).

requestedCapabilities.description:
Names from the capability registry. Unknown entries are not an error
and simply do not appear in `grantedCapabilities` — which is why this
is a list of free strings rather than of registry names.

ClientInfo.description:
Client identification inside `initialize` params (SS1.4.1). Diagnostics
and telemetry attribution only; never an authority claim (SS1.10).

CommandAcceptedResult.description:
The uniform SS3.1.2 command acknowledgement: admission only, never an
outcome. `session/compact` alone may answer `"noop"`; every other command
answers `"accepted"`.

status.description: `"accepted"` for every admitted command (SS3.1.2; closed vocabulary).

CommandAckStatus.description:
The ack-status vocabulary (`tdd.md` SS3.1/SS3.1.2): `"accepted"` for every
admitted command; `session/compact` alone may answer `"noop"`. Closed:
SS3.1.2 names exactly these two values, so SDK clients get a discriminated
type and validation catches a wrong status (PR #21550 review) — and a
client that received a third value would have been told nothing it can act
on, unlike [`TurnStartDisposition`], where "acked, not otherwise
classified" is a usable reading.

CommandStatus.description:
The SS3.1.2 ack `status`: `accepted` for every admitted command.
`session/compact` is the one method that may additionally answer `noop`
([`crate::method::runtime::CompactStatus`]); no other command uses another
status (tdd SS3.1.2).

CompactStatus.description:
`session/compact`'s ack status (tdd SS3.7): the one method that may answer
`noop` in addition to the SS3.1.2 `accepted`. A noop is a success, not an
error, and it is durably settled like any other outcome.

CompactionOutcome.description: Compaction outcome (tdd SS4.5.10, the SS3.7 vocabulary). Open.

CompactionTrigger.description: What initiated a compaction (tdd SS4.5.10). Open.

ContextPressureLevel.description:
Context pressure level (tdd SS4.6.6): hard threshold first, both
inclusive `>=`. Open.

ContextUsage.description:
The SS4.9.1 snapshot `contextUsage` block: the latest
`(windowTokens, usedTokens, pressure)` triple; the snapshot member is
`null` until the fold's generation chain holds a tracked anchor AND the
current basis is present (absent is never fabricated).

usedTokens.description: Counted-once occupancy at the latest provider-reported fact.

windowTokens.description: The effective context-window size; absent when the basis has no limit.

CumulativeTokenUsage.description: Session running totals of counted-once usage (tdd SS4.6.5).

EffectiveApprovalModeState.description:
The effective approval-mode projection (`EffectiveApprovalModeState`,
tdd SS5.12): the same object `session/setApprovalMode` returns as
`effectiveMode` and the `Session` object carries as `approvalMode`.

lastCommandId.description: The command that last set it; `null` when no command did.

EffectiveModel.description: The latest effective-model fact in the snapshot (tdd SS4.9.1).

providerId.description: The selected provider; `null` when the selection names none.

ErrorData.description:
The optional `error.data` object (SS1.6). All members additive-optional;
`kind` is always present when `data` is.

alignedNextOffset.description:
The next provable UTF-8 boundary on a misaligned text-media
`item/readOutput` read (`-32602` `invalidParams`, FR-016b/D-17214-2):
absent when no boundary is provable from the stored bytes ahead.

anchor.description:
The rejected anchor value on `notFound`/`missingAnchor` and the
`-32042` boundary arms (SS4.7.3, SS4.11); on `-32042` it is served
as an explicit `null` when the request named no concrete anchor
(spec 208 FM-005).

capability.description:
The missing capability, on `capabilityRequired` errors. Typed on the
grantable registry, so `rawLog` is outside the v1 domain and joins it
as an additive open-enum extension when SS6 un-defers (TEST-009).

capacity.description: The configured command-admission bound, on `backpressured` errors.

commandId.description:
The rejected command's identifier, on `commandRejected` errors. The
ratified v1 contract pairs it with `reason`
(specs/13929-msp-activation/tdd.md SS3.6 admission-failure table and
its `-32030` example), so a client can settle the exact command it
sent without parsing the message string.

earliestCursor.description:
The oldest servable view position on `viewTruncated` (`-32040`,
SS4.11); served as an explicit `null` when nothing before the head
is servable — the null is present on the wire, never a dropped key
(spec 208 FM-005 / Scenario 6.2).

kind.description: The stable camelCase category clients branch on.

latestBoundaryCursor.description:
The latest installed boundary's view cursor on the `-32042` arms —
always present in the `-32042` JSON and explicitly `null` when no
boundary exists (SS4.11, FM-004).

limitBytes.description: The exceeded byte limit, on `inputTooLarge` errors.

reason.description:
Failure detail vocabulary (e.g. `"missingAnchor"` on `notFound` for a
missing view-cursor anchor).

retryable.description:
Whether retrying can succeed (e.g. `overloaded`). When present,
overrides the error table row's `retryable` default for this code.

sessionId.description: Session identity on errors whose lookup is session-scoped.

userInputId.description: User-input prompt identity on SS5.10 errors.

viewCursor.description: The blocked view position on `pageEventTooLarge` errors.

ErrorKind.description:
A stable `error.data.kind` category (SS1.6): camelCase, the value clients
branch on. Open: SS2–SS5 lanes add kinds additively as their methods land
(Appendix B already registers them), and the spec's edge-case rule makes a
new `kind` additive only because this domain is declared open.

ErrorObject.description: The `error` member of an error response (SS1.2 §2.4).

code.description:
Registry code (Appendix B). Typed as a plain integer on the wire; the
value domain is the registry below (INV-018).

message.description: Human-readable message. Never a branch point (SS1.6).

ErrorResponse.description:
An error response frame (SS1.2 §2.4). Exactly one of `result` or `error`
appears on a response; this type is the `error` half.

id.description:
Echo of the request id; `null` **only** for an unrecoverable parse
error whose offending id could not be recovered (SS1.3). Always
serialized, so `None` renders as `null` rather than being omitted —
required-but-nullable (see [`require_nullable_id`]).

ForkCutPoint.description:
Where a fork cuts the source history (tdd SS2.5.3). Turn ids are used
instead of counts because ids stay stable across compaction and concurrent
appends while indices do not.

lastTurnId.description:
The last completed turn to copy, inclusive. Naming an in-progress or
unknown turn fails `forkBoundaryInvalid`.

ForkProvenance.description:
Fork provenance folded from the durable `session.fork.created` record
(`ForkProvenance`, tdd SS2.4).

commandId.description: The `commandId` of the `session/fork` that created it.

cutCursor.description:
An **opaque provenance string** preserved verbatim from the durable
record. Display-only — not one of the SS6.2 cursor families: clients
MUST NOT parse it and no method accepts it (tdd SS2.4).

cutExplicit.description: Whether the fork named an explicit cut point.

sessionId.description: The source session this fork was cut from.

Goal.description:
The session goal block (tdd SS4.6.2, mirrors the runtime's goal state,
camelCased). `status` and `percentComplete` are carried **verbatim** —
out-of-contract status strings and >100 percents pass through; display
clamping is the renderer's job.

status.description:
Goal status, verbatim from the durable goal state (free string by
design: out-of-contract values pass through).

HistoryMode.description:
What history a lifecycle result actually served (tdd SS2.5.2). Open on the
client side: report-what-was-served means a client treats an unknown mode
as "page it yourself".

HistoryNoneReason.description:
Why a result served `history.mode: "none"` — spec 208 FM-005's typed
unavailability (tdd SS2.5.2; D-050). Open on the client side: an absent
(older server) or unknown (newer server) value decodes conservatively as
an unknown reason, and `viewCursor` text never substitutes for it
(spec 208 INV-19734-1).

HistoryPreference.description:
The `history` request preference of `session/resume` (tdd SS2.5.2). The
forced values downgrade `anchored` → `inline` → `snapshot` → `none`; under
`auto` the full rung order is anchoredSnapshot → inline → snapshot →
elided snapshot → none.

IfBusy.description:
Disposition when a turn is already running (tdd SS3.2). The wire default
is `queue`: an SDK caller who has not looked at session state should not
silently mutate an in-flight turn.

capabilities.description: Capability posture; absent means all defaults.

experimentalApi.description: Echo of the effective negotiated experimental setting.

grantedCapabilities.description:
Subset of the requested capabilities, plus policy-implicit grants.
Fixed for the connection lifetime (INV-009).

museHome.description: Absolute path of the muse home directory.

schema.description: Envelope schema version and stable-surface fingerprint.

sessionDurability.description:
Whether this host persists its sessions (SS2.13). Optional so the
addition is additive under SS1.5.4; a v1 host always sends it, and a
client reads absent as `durable` because no server that omits it has
the ephemeral profile.

userAgent.description: Exact user-agent string presented to upstream model providers.

Item.description:
One transcript item at one revision (tdd SS4.4.1 common fields plus the
per-kind fields of SS4.5.2–4.5.10, all optional and owned by the kind
their doc names). `item/started`, `item/updated`, and `item/completed`
carry the full object; `item/delta` appends to it by field path.

approvalId.description:
`toolCall`: the approval that gated this call (tdd SS5); join key for
the approval view events.

args.description:
`toolCall`: the model-authored argument JSON, **verbatim**; clients
parse. Verbatim keeps the fold byte-deterministic and survives
model-emitted almost-JSON (tdd SS4.5.5).

attachments.description:
`userMessage`: image attachment metadata only — base64 payloads are
not echoed back on the view (tdd SS4.5.2).

background.description:
`toolCall`: `true` once the task was durably backgrounded; delivered
via `item/updated`.

backgroundInitiator.description:
`toolCall`: who backgrounded the task; absent on pre-split records —
never inferred (tdd SS4.5.5).

childSessionId.description:
`subagent`/`reminderChild`: the child's own session id, readable via
`session/read`/`view/page` — child transcript drill-down without a
second protocol (tdd SS4.5.7).

childSessionLogPath.description:
`reminderChild`: parent-session-dir-relative child log path; absent
when no filesystem log.

children.description:
`workflow`: folded per-child state, keyed by `(childId, attempt)`,
re-emitted whole on every change — the item `revision` is the
ordering guard (tdd SS4.5.8).

commandId.description:
`userMessage`/`userShell`: the submitting command — multi-client UIs
de-duplicate their local echo on it.

controlStatus.description:
`subagent`: camelCased `SubagentControlStatus` (open enum); `status`
stays the generic item vocabulary.

displayText.description:
`userMessage`: presentation form (tdd SS3.2); absent when the client
sent none.

exitCode.description: `userShell`: the process exit code, when it exited by code.

exitSignal.description:
`userShell`: the terminating signal NUMBER, when signalled (e.g. 9) —
the durable payload verbatim; nothing maps numbers to names, and the
fold never invents one.

failureKind.description:
`toolCall`: machine-readable failure class (`TaskFailureKind`,
snake_case verbatim — durable runtime vocabulary, the SS1.6 casing
exemption).

fallbackText.description:
Server-provided one-line human summary any kind MAY carry, for
generic rendering of kinds a client does not recognize; new kinds
SHOULD carry it during their first release cycle (tdd SS4.10).

itemId.description:
Bare UUIDv7; the item's identity across its whole lifecycle. Identity
rule (tdd SS4.4.1): the task id for task-backed kinds
(`toolCall`, `subagent`), the pre-minted commit `message_id` for
delta-streamed kinds (`agentMessage`, `reasoning`), and the opening
durable record's event id for everything else. Opaque to clients.

kind.description:
The item kind (open enum): clients MUST render unknown kinds
generically — kind name plus `status` plus `fallbackText` (tdd
SS4.10).

message.description: `workflow`: the reconciled terminal message, set on completion.

modelVisibleContent.description:
`toolCall`: rich content the model saw beyond text; base64 is not
inlined on the view (tdd SS4.5.5).

outputRef.description:
`toolCall`/`userShell`: stored-output reference; fetch the full bytes
via `item/readOutput` (served by #208).

providerItemId.description:
`reasoning`: provider reasoning item id (e.g. `rs_...`), for
provider-side correlation.

reason.description:
`compaction`: noop/failure reason, verbatim (snake_case durable
vocabulary, e.g. `"no_compactable_history"`).

recordedAt.description:
RFC3339 timestamp of the item's driving durable record. Absent on
ephemeral-opened items until first durable re-emission (tdd SS4.4.1).

retracted.description:
`userMessage`: `true` after an accepted retract (tdd SS4.5.1);
re-emitted via `item/updated`.

revision.description:
Integer >= 1, strictly monotonic per item; apply rule is
replace-iff-higher. `item/delta` never bumps it (tdd SS4.4.1).

status.description:
Open enum; terminal = anything other than `"inProgress"`. Unknown
values MUST be treated as terminal-unknown and rendered generically
(tdd SS4.4.1).

steered.description:
`userMessage`: `true` when injected mid-turn via `turn/steer` or
`ifBusy: "steer"`; absent otherwise.

summarizedThrough.description:
`compaction`: opaque provenance string naming the compaction
boundary. A compaction-anchored read anchor since D-029 (2026-08-12):
accepted by `session/resume` and `view/page` (wire shape and
validation are the #208 lane's). Still opaque — clients relay it,
never parse it (tdd SS4.5.10).

summary.description:
`reasoning`: one entry per summary part; part *n* streams via
`item/delta` field `"summary.n"` (part boundary = index change).

text.description:
`userMessage`: the prompt text as submitted. `agentMessage`: the
accumulated reply, streamed via `item/delta` field `"text"`.
`reasoning`: raw committed reasoning text where the provider exposes
it (never streamed in v1, tdd SS4.5.4).

tokensAfter.description: `compaction`: token budget snapshot after, when measured.

tokensBefore.description: `compaction`: token budget snapshot before, when measured.

truncated.description:
`true` when the server's per-surface text budget saturated a streamed
surface (`agentMessage.text`, `reasoning.summary[*]`,
`toolCall.visibleOutput`, `userShell.visibleOutput`); the durable
full text remains in the log (tdd SS4.5.4).

turnId.description:
The owning turn (== the submitting `commandId` for fresh turns, tdd
SS3.1.4). `null` only for `userShell` — the one kind outside a turn
(tdd SS4.5.6).

usage.description:
`subagent`: **transitive** observed usage — the child and its own
descendants; updated in place, absent until first observation; never
folded into `session/tokenUsage.cumulative` (tdd SS4.6.5).

visibleOutput.description:
`toolCall`/`userShell`: bounded transcript-visible result text
(budget per tdd SS4.5.4); streams via `item/delta` field `"output"`.

workflowRunId.description:
`subagent`/`workflow`: the owning durable workflow run id (opaque
string — not a UUID family).

ItemCompletedParams.description:
`item/completed` params (tdd SS4.3): the item reached its terminal state
— the authoritative final object. Always cites a durable `sourceRange`
(tdd SS4.2). Clients MUST accept `item/completed` for an `itemId` they
never saw `item/started` for (single-shot kinds; after a gap fill; tdd
SS4.4.1).

item.description: The full item at its terminal revision.

sourceRange.description: The durable records this event folded from.

viewCursor.description: Opaque, strictly monotonic view cursor (tdd SS4.1).

ItemDeltaParams.description:
`item/delta` params (tdd SS4.3.1): a UTF-8-safe streaming append to an
open item's field. Ephemeral-sourced by definition: this params object
has **no** `sourceRange` member at all (spec 14653 INV-009 — the schema
enforces the exemption). Deltas never bump `revision`.

delta.description:
The appended text; concatenation of a field path's deltas in cursor
order equals that field's value on `item/completed` unless the
surface saturated (spec 14653 INV-005).

field.description:
Dotted field path the append targets (`"summary.0"`, `"output"`,
...); absent means `"text"` (tdd SS4.3.1).

itemId.description: The open item being appended to.

viewCursor.description: Opaque, strictly monotonic view cursor (tdd SS4.1).

ItemKind.description:
The nine v1 item kinds (tdd SS4.5.2–4.5.10). Open: a new kind is additive
evolution, and clients MUST render unknown kinds generically (tdd
SS4.10).

ItemStartedParams.description:
`item/started` params (tdd SS4.3): a new item opened on the transcript.
`sourceRange` is absent when the item opens on an ephemeral record (the
delta-streamed kinds); the item's authoritative open is re-stated by its
durable-sourced `item/completed` (tdd SS4.2).

sourceRange.description:
The durable records this event folded from; absent on an
ephemeral-sourced open (spec 14653 INV-009).

viewCursor.description: Opaque, strictly monotonic view cursor (tdd SS4.1).

ItemStatus.description:
Item status (tdd SS4.4.1). Open; terminal = anything other than
`"inProgress"`, and unknown values are terminal-unknown, rendered
generically.

ItemUpdatedParams.description:
`item/updated` params (tdd SS4.4.2): an open item changed non-terminally
in a way deltas cannot express — the full item re-emitted at a higher
revision (apply rule: replace iff higher).

item.description: The full item at a higher revision.

sourceRange.description: The durable records this event folded from.

viewCursor.description: Opaque, strictly monotonic view cursor (tdd SS4.1).

MessageAttachment.description:
`userMessage` image attachment metadata (tdd SS4.5.2): metadata only —
the durable bytes live in the log and are reachable on the raw altitude.

type.description:
Attachment type, `"image"` in v1 (free string: attachment vocabulary
grows additively with the runtime's intake surface).

ModelCatalogEntry.description:
One visible catalog row (tdd SS3.10). Catalog rows marked hidden never
reach the wire, so a client cannot select one.

contextLimit.description: Context limit; `null` when the catalog source declared nothing.

cost.description: Cost block; `null` when the catalog source declared nothing.

description.description: Description; `null` when the catalog source declared nothing.

isActive.description:
Marks the session's effective model when `sessionId` was supplied. May
be false for every row — a client MUST NOT assume exactly one.

isDefault.description: Marks the catalog's default row. May be false for every row.

outputLimit.description: Output limit; `null` when the catalog source declared nothing.

profileId.description: Provider profile; `null` when the catalog source declared nothing.

releaseDate.description: Release date; `null` when the catalog source declared nothing.

ModelCatalogSource.description:
Where a model catalog came from (tdd SS3.10). **Open**: an unrecognized
value is an unknown source, not an error.

ModelChangeSource.description: What drove a model selection (tdd SS4.6.1). Open.

ModelCost.description:
Per-1M-token catalog cost, carried **verbatim** for display and never
rounded or re-formatted by the host (tdd SS3.10). Cost arithmetic stays
client-local view math.

currency.description: Currency; nullable — today's catalogs are USD.

ModelListParams.description:
`model/list` params (tdd SS3.10): the discovery half of the model-picker
gesture. **A query, not a command** — no `commandId`, no durable intake
record, no view event.

sessionId.description:
When present, the row matching that session's effective model is
flagged `isActive`. When absent, no row is active — a client may list
before it has a session (tdd SS3.10).

ModelListResult.description:
`model/list` result (tdd SS3.10). A snapshot at call time: v1 has no
catalog subscription. `models` MAY be empty — a build shipped with no
bundled models is a supported configuration.

source.description:
Where the catalog came from — how a client tells a live provider
catalog from a test fake and labels it honestly.

ModelSelection.description: A model selection (tdd SS3.8). Empty strings are normalized to absent.

profileId.description:
Provider profile. Omitted and explicit `null` both mean "no profile"
(#23468).

ModelVisibleContent.description:
Rich content the model saw beyond text (tdd SS4.5.5,
`ModelVisibleToolContent`): metadata only — fetch bytes via
`item/readOutput` when an `outputRef` exists.

sourceToolName.description: The tool that produced the content.

type.description:
Content type, `"image"` in v1 (free string, grows with the durable
vocabulary).

Notification.description:
A notification frame, either direction (SS1.2 §2.2). No `id`; a
notification is never answered.

params.description: Method-specific parameters; omitted entirely when empty.

OutputRef.description:
Stored-output reference (tdd SS4.5.5): the camelCased fold of the durable
`ToolOutputRef`. The fetch path is `item/readOutput` (#208).

availability.description: Whether the bytes are servable (tdd SS4.5.5).

kind.description:
The stored output's kind, verbatim durable vocabulary (e.g.
`"tool_output"`; snake_case per the SS1.6 casing exemption).

OutputRefAvailability.description:
Whether a stored output's bytes are servable (tdd SS4.5.5). Open —
durable runtime vocabulary may grow additively.

PendingApprovalPointer.description:
A pending approval in the snapshot: the SS2.5.2 pointer shape plus the
gated `itemId` when one exists (tdd SS4.9.1).

itemId.description: The parked item, when one exists.

viewCursor.description: The cursor the approval opened at.

PendingRequestKind.description:
The `pendingRequests` discriminator (tdd SS2.5.2). Open enum, v1 values
`approval` and `userInput`.

PendingRequestPointer.description:
A late-joiner pointer at an unsettled server-initiated request
(tdd SS2.5.2, SS2.2.1). The full payloads arrive as re-issued
server-to-client requests right after a `session/resume` response
(tdd SS5.6); `session/read` never re-issues them (tdd SS2.5.5).

**A second E4 instance, RULED with E4 (#22785, owner, 2026-08-26): the
flat discriminated-object precedent is accepted for this type too, on the
`ApprovalSubject` precedent, with the serialized JSON unchanged. A strict
union node kind may be funded later; if it is, it must cover both this
type and `TurnInputPart`.** SS2.5.2 ratifies two
kind-discriminated entry shapes (`{kind: "approval", approvalId,
viewCursor}` / `{kind: "userInput", userInputId, viewCursor}`); this is one
flat object with both ids optional, so the published schema accepts
`{"kind":"approval","userInputId":…}` and an entry carrying no id at all.
The v1 model names no object-variant union (the `ApprovalSubject`
precedent, followed for `TurnInputPart`), and this instance differs from
that one in a way the ruling should see: `kind` here is an OPEN enum,
where `TurnInputPart.type` is closed.

viewCursor.description: The cursor the request opened at.

PendingUserInputPointer.description: A pending user-input prompt in the snapshot (tdd SS4.9.1, SS5.10).

itemId.description: The parked item, when one exists.

viewCursor.description: The cursor the prompt opened at.

PlatformFamily.description:
The server runtime's platform family (SS1.4.1); may differ from the
client's. Closed: SS1.4.1 fixes the value set, so widening it is a
deliberate, gate-visible protocol change rather than a silent addition
(a later `Closed`→`Open` flip is itself additive, data-model.md §5.2).

PlatformOs.description:
The server's operating system (SS1.4.1). Closed, for the same reason as
[`PlatformFamily`].

ReasoningEffort.description:
The reasoning-effort tier sampled at submission (tdd SS3.2, SS3.3). The
**same closed tier vocabulary** on both the fresh-turn and steer lanes,
spelled identically; invalid tiers are invalid params. `none` is a tier of
the vocabulary (ask for no reasoning), not a way to say "unset".

RecordPosition.description:
One end of a [`SourceRange`]: a record's event id and its sequence number
within the stream (tdd SS4.2).

sequence.description: The record's sequence number within its stream.

id.description: Client-chosen id, unique among that client's in-flight requests.

params.description: Method-specific parameters; omitted entirely when empty, never `null`.

RequestId.description:
A request id (SS1.3): client-chosen string or integer. `1` and `"1"` do
not compare equal; each direction owns its own id space.

SchemaInfo.description:
The `schema` pair in [`InitializeResult`] (SS1.4.1, SS1.5.3). `version`
is the wire **envelope** schema version — distinct from the session-view
`schemaVersion`, the raw-log `schema_version`, and the 0.x/1.0 stability
posture, which is not on the wire at all (INV-006a).

fingerprint.description:
`sha256:<64 lower hex>` content hash of this server binary's
stable-surface bundle (INV-003). A mismatch is a warning condition,
not an error (SS1.4.1).

version.description:
Envelope schema version; `1` in v1, expected to stay `1` for a long
time (SS1.4.1).

Session.description:
The session object every lifecycle method returns or lists (tdd SS2.4).

Additive-optional evolution applies: clients must ignore unknown fields.

activeTurnId.description:
The `turnId` of the current foreground turn when `status` is
`running`, and `null` when the session is idle (tdd SS2.4).

**Required-nullable, per the owner ruling on #22946** ("approve
required-nullable", review comment `r3863946961`, 2026-08-26). Both
production writers hard-code `"activeTurnId": null`
(`session/start/commit_load.rs` for `session/start`,
`session/snapshot.rs` feeding resume/read/list/fork) and nothing
strips it, so this is what the binary emits and what SS2.4's example
spells. The optional-absent shape published it as plain `string` and
REJECTED every idle `Session` frame the host sent — the #19923 defect
class this PR exists to close.

E5's original evidence for optional-absent ("every committed
transcript shows the omission") was wrong: those transcripts are
hand-authored fixtures, not host recordings. They are corrected in the
same change under the ruling's SS1.5 `regenerationJustification`.

approvalMode.description:
The folded effective approval mode. **Additive-optional**: a Session
object that omits it means the host has not folded a mode, which is
why the index-derived `session/list` entry may legitimately omit it
(tdd SS2.4, SS5.12).

createdAt.description:
RFC3339. For a fork this is the fork session id's UUIDv7 mint instant
(tdd SS2.4).

forkedFrom.description: `null` for root sessions; fork provenance otherwise (tdd SS2.4).

modelId.description: The winning metadata fold's model; `null` when that record omits it.

path.description:
Absolute path of the session's durable log; non-nullable. Under the
ephemeral session profile it is the **empty string**, meaning "no
durable log exists" (tdd SS2.13.2) — the one value a client must not
hand to a filesystem call.

providerId.description: The winning metadata fold's provider; `null` when that record omits it.

status.description:
Load state as this host knows it; `session/list` reports `notLoaded`
for sessions loaded by *other* hosts (tdd SS2.4).

turnCount.description: Completed-turn count from the session view fold (tdd SS2.4).

workspaceRoot.description:
The winning metadata fold's workspace root; `null` when that record
omits it — absent is never fabricated (tdd SS2.4).

SessionApprovalModeChangedParams.description:
`session/approvalModeChanged` params (tdd SS5.12): the fold of the
durable approval-mode reconfigure audit fact — every accepted change
writes one; a mode flip without an audit fact is a runtime bug by design.

clientName.description:
The requesting client's `clientInfo.name` (tdd SS1.4.1), recorded on
the audit fact.

sourceRange.description: The durable records this event folded from.

viewCursor.description: Opaque, strictly monotonic view cursor (tdd SS4.1).

SessionBranchChangedParams.description:
`session/branchChanged` params (tdd SS4.6.4): a durable workspace-branch
observation landed.

branch.description:
The observed branch; `null` on a detached-HEAD observation — a fact,
not "unchanged" (tdd SS4.6.4).

sourceRange.description: The durable records this event folded from.

vcs.description:
The detected version-control system; absent when no repository was
detected.

viewCursor.description: Opaque, strictly monotonic view cursor (tdd SS4.1).

SessionCompactParams.description:
`session/compact` params (tdd SS3.7): manually compact the session's
conversation context — the `/compact` gesture. Compaction runs
asynchronously; the ack is admission only.

turnId.description:
The run whose context to compact. Omit and the server resolves the
session's current/latest run; a session with no resolvable run rejects
with `commandRejected` reason `missing_run` (tdd SS3.7).

SessionCompactResult.description:
`session/compact` result (tdd SS3.7). Failures *after* admission
(`summarizer_failed`, `install_rejected`, `cancelled`) are not wire errors
— they arrive as the compaction's terminal view event.

reason.description:
Why the command was a noop, e.g. `no_compactable_history`. Present on
a `noop` status (tdd SS3.7).

SessionConfig.description:
`session/start`'s reserved `config` object (tdd SS2.5.1): no members in
v1.

SS2.5.1 also ratifies "unknown keys are rejected, not ignored". That is
#22785 E6b, ruled and NOT exported: spec 206 INV-015 forbids it
categorically and TEST-024 enforces that. The model carries the opt-in
mechanism; this type does not opt in, so the published surface is
unchanged. See [#23456](https://github.com/mslsrc/tbh/issues/23456).

SessionContextUsageParams.description:
`session/contextUsage` params (tdd SS4.6.6, #14405): context-window
pressure — the counted-once occupancy at the latest provider-reported
durable fact, joined with the host's pressure basis. Replace wholesale;
emitted only when the `(windowTokens, usedTokens, pressure)` triple
changes value (identical adoptions emit nothing).

pressure.description: Server-computed pressure level over the basis thresholds.

sourceRange.description: The durable records this event folded from.

usedTokens.description:
Counted-once prompt tokens (#8803) plus output tokens of the driving
record, saturating — the honest occupancy floor.

viewCursor.description: Opaque, strictly monotonic view cursor (tdd SS4.1).

SessionDurability.description:
Whether this host writes its sessions to disk (SS1.4.1, SS2.13). A
property of the host process, fixed at construction and identical for
every session and every connection it serves — never requested, granted,
or negotiated, which is why it is not a capability. Open: the
unrepresented degraded state (#14401) has candidate resolutions that add a
third value here, so closed would make that a breaking change.

cutPoint.description:
Copy history through a completed turn, inclusive. Omitted means "all
completed turns" (tdd SS2.5.3).

excludeItems.description:
Skip inline history in the result and page it later — same as
`session/resume` (tdd SS2.5.3).

SessionForkResult.description:
`session/fork` result (tdd SS2.5.3): the `session/resume` envelope for the
**new** session, whose `session.forkedFrom` carries the provenance.

session.description: The new fork session, carrying `forkedFrom` provenance.

viewCursor.description: The new session's view head.

SessionGoalChangedParams.description:
`session/goalChanged` params (tdd SS4.6.2): the projected goal block's
value changed — identical adoptions emit nothing (the change gate), and
an explicit `null` clears. Replace wholesale; `null` never means
unchanged.

goal.description: The full current goal block, or `null` to clear.

sourceRange.description: The durable records this event folded from.

viewCursor.description: Opaque, strictly monotonic view cursor (tdd SS4.1).

SessionHistory.description:
The `history` envelope shared by `session/resume`, `session/fork`, and
`session/read` (tdd SS2.5.2).

items.description: The full folded item array when `mode` is `inline`; `null` otherwise.

mode.description: What was actually served — never what was asked for (tdd SS2.5.2).

noneReason.description:
Why no history was served — sent exactly when `mode` is `"none"`
(tdd SS2.5.2; D-050, spec 208 INV-19734-1).

snapshot.description:
The folded view state when `mode` is `snapshot` or `anchoredSnapshot`;
`null` otherwise.

SessionListParams.description: `session/list` params (tdd SS2.5.4). Read-only; never touches leases.

cursor.description:
Opaque page cursor from a prior result. Page cursors are a distinct
opaque-string family from view cursors and stream cursors, valid only
for re-issuing the same listing (tdd SS2.5.4). Omitted and explicit
`null` both mean "first page" (#23468).

limit.description:
Page size; default 50, max 200 — the cap is published under #22785
E6c (owner-ruled 2026-08-26).

updatedAfter.description: Only sessions with log activity after this RFC3339 instant.

workspaceRoot.description: Only sessions whose metadata workspace root equals this path.

nextCursor.description: The next page's cursor; `null` on the last page.

SessionModelChangedParams.description:
`session/modelChanged` params (tdd SS4.6.1): a durable model-selection
record landed (tdd SS3.8).

providerId.description: The selected provider; `null` when the selection names none.

sourceRange.description: The durable records this event folded from.

viewCursor.description: Opaque, strictly monotonic view cursor (tdd SS4.1).

SessionReadParams.description:
`session/read` params (tdd SS2.5.5): read one stored session **without
attaching** — no writer lease, no load, no subscription, no
`SessionResumed` record.

excludeItems.description:
Metadata-only unless you ask: `false` carries the folded item history.
Same name and polarity as `session/resume`/`session/fork`; only the
default differs — here it is `true` (tdd SS2.5.5).

SessionReadResult.description:
`session/read` result (tdd SS2.5.5). The `viewCursor` is the fold head at
read time — a point-in-time read, immediately stale if a foreign host is
appending.

pendingRequests.description:
The same pointer shape as `session/resume`. Because `session/read`
never subscribes this is a point-in-time log read only: no requests
are re-issued after it (tdd SS2.5.5).

viewCursor.description: The fold head at read time.

commandId.description:
The SS2.5 idempotency handle (UUIDv7). A resume that loads a session
writes a durable `SessionResumed` record.

cursor.description:
A view cursor previously observed by this client — or an observed
`summarizedThrough` compaction anchor (tdd SS4.5.10, D-029). When
present the server returns only the suffix and `history.mode` is
`none` (tdd SS2.5.2). Omitted and explicit `null` both mean "no
cursor" (#23468).

excludeItems.description:
Return only session metadata and live resume state; page history
separately with `view/page`. Default `false` (tdd SS2.5.2).

history.description:
History mode preference, default `auto`. A PREFERENCE, not a budget
override: when the requested mode does not fit the history budget the
server downgrades it and `history.mode` reports what was actually
served (tdd SS2.5.2). Ignored when `cursor` or `excludeItems` makes it
moot.

pendingRequests.description: The late-joiner pointer set; empty when nothing is pending.

viewCursor.description: The session view head; the connection is subscribed after it.

SessionSetApprovalModeParams.description:
`session/setApprovalMode` params (tdd SS5.12): switch the session's
approval enforcement mode mid-session. A standard SS3 command.

**Select, never create.** A client may *select* a mode the host's
configuration already defines; it may not construct one, supply inline
rules, or otherwise describe a policy on the wire — which is why
[`ApprovalMode`] is closed.

mode.description:
The preconfigured mode to select. The requesting actor is recorded
from the connection's `clientInfo.name` (tdd SS1.4.1).

SessionSetApprovalModeResult.description:
`session/setApprovalMode` result (tdd SS5.12). Applies next-action — an
in-flight tool action's pending approval is not retroactively decided by a
mode change.

effectiveMode.description:
The folded effective-mode projection — the same object the `Session`
carries as `approvalMode` (tdd SS2.4, SS5.12).

SessionSetModelParams.description:
`session/setModel` params (tdd SS3.8): the model-picker gesture. The
selection is durable and applies to subsequent model calls.

SessionSetModelResult.description:
`session/setModel` result (tdd SS3.8). If a turn is running the selection
is admitted now and applied at the next model-call boundary; the ack does
not wait for that boundary.

approvalMode.description:
The session's starting approval mode; server default when omitted or
explicit `null` — both spellings select the default (#23468).
Select, never create — the value names a mode the host's configuration
already defines (tdd SS2.5.1, SS5.12). This is the only surface that
declares a non-interactive run's policy (tdd SS5.11, D-008).

commandId.description:
The SS2.5 idempotency handle (UUIDv7). Required; the server never
mints one.

config.description:
Reserved for per-session overrides owned by a future Configuration
section, which is why [`SessionConfig`] declares no members.

modelId.description: Initial model; server default when omitted.

providerId.description:
Initial provider routing; server default when omitted or explicit
`null` — both spellings select the default (#23468).

sessionId.description:
Exact identity for this new root session. When omitted the server
mints a UUIDv7. This field never selects an existing session: a
retained or reserved id is rejected `commandRejected` with reason
`session_id_conflict` (tdd SS2.5.1).

workspaceRoot.description: Absolute path, folded into the first metadata record.

viewCursor.description:
The session view head after the start fold; the connection is
subscribed and receives every view event after this cursor. A
deduplicated retry returns this same result (tdd SS2.5.1).

SessionTodoListChangedParams.description:
`session/todoListChanged` params (tdd SS4.6.3): a `TodoSnapshotUpdated`
record landed. Replace the whole list on every event; an empty `items`
array is a cleared list, not a no-op.

items.description: The full todo list, replaced wholesale.

revision.description:
The snapshot revision. Diagnostics only, never an ordering guard —
`viewCursor` orders (tdd SS4.6.3).

sourceRange.description: The durable records this event folded from.

sourceTool.description: The tool that produced the snapshot, verbatim.

viewCursor.description: Opaque, strictly monotonic view cursor (tdd SS4.1).

SessionTokenUsageParams.description:
`session/tokenUsage` params (tdd SS4.6.5): one per model completion that
reports usage. Carries the raw counters verbatim plus the server-derived
counted-once `promptTokens`/`totalTokens` (#8803: clients display and sum
these and never re-derive the provider's cache convention) and the
session `cumulative` block. Accumulate-only: `cumulative` never goes
backward.

cumulative.description:
Session running totals at this cursor; the fold owns the
accumulation. Subagent/workflow-child usage is never folded in — it
rides the owning items (tdd SS4.6.5).

finishReason.description: Provider finish reason when reported (open vocabulary, verbatim).

modelId.description:
The effective model that produced this usage; `null` on pre-schema
records — never back-filled, an unpriced leg (tdd SS4.6.5).

promptTokens.description:
Prompt tokens counted exactly once under the provider's cache
convention (#8803). Server-derived; deterministic — the provider is
in the log.

sourceRange.description: The durable records this event folded from.

turnId.description: The turn whose model call completed.

usage.description: Raw counters verbatim from the durable record.

viewCursor.description: Opaque, strictly monotonic view cursor (tdd SS4.1).

SessionUserShellParams.description:
`session/userShell` params (tdd SS3.9): run a user-initiated shell command
in the session's workspace — the TUI's `!` escape hatch.
**Capability-gated**: the connection must negotiate `userShell` at
`initialize`, and the whole justification is the SS1.10 spawn boundary.

SessionUserShellResult.description:
`session/userShell` result (tdd SS3.9): immediate. The shell runs off the
command worker so a long command cannot stall the command plane; the
output arrives as the `userShell` item's terminal view event.

SnapshotAnchor.description: The compaction boundary an anchored snapshot is anchored at (tdd SS2.5.2).

boundaryCursor.description: The view cursor of the boundary's `compaction` event.

summarizedThrough.description: The boundary's opaque compaction anchor (tdd SS4.5.10).

SnapshotState.description:
The complete folded view at the snapshot cursor (tdd SS4.9.1).

Additive-optional evolution applies exactly as everywhere else; unknown
members MUST be ignored, and preserved if re-serialized.

**One served site does not satisfy this type today, escalated under
#22785 (E8).** The genesis snapshot rung serves
`state: {"items": [...]}` alone
(`tbh-session-view-serve`'s `materialized_fold.rs`, the
`select_genesis_history` call), while the anchored rung serves the full
folded state. A schema-validating client resuming with
`{"history": "snapshot"}` against the real fold therefore sees the other
required members missing. The fix is a serving change in the #208/#14653
lane (serialize the `SessionViewState` the genesis path already folds, as
the anchored path does) plus its own RED against the real fold; it is not
a shape change here, because SS4.9.1 ratifies this shape.

activeTurn.description: The running foreground turn; `null` when none is running.

approvalMode.description:
The effective approval mode at this cursor — the same object the
`Session` carries (tdd SS2.4, SS5.12).

branch.description: Latest branch observation; `null` when no fact has landed.

contextUsage.description:
The latest `(windowTokens, usedTokens, pressure)` triple. SS4.9.1
says "`null`/absent" and SS4.9.2's worked example OMITS the member;
the binary omits it too, so this is the absent arm — the four
siblings above are present-null in the same frame. INV-017 admits one
or the other, never both; escalated under #22785.

effectiveModel.description: Latest effective model; `null` when no fact has landed.

goal.description: Latest goal block; `null` when no fact has landed.

items.description:
Every item, in first-opened order, each at its latest revision at the
snapshot cursor. One schema per kind, shared with the notification
item object — which is what makes snapshot+suffix a pure splice
(tdd SS4.9.1).

pendingApprovals.description: The pending-approval half of the pending set.

pendingUserInputs.description: The pending-user-input half of the pending set.

queuedTurns.description: Admitted-but-not-launched submits, in launch order (tdd SS3.1.4).

todoList.description: Latest todo list; `null` when no fact has landed.

tokenUsage.description:
The `cumulative` block of the last `session/tokenUsage` event; zeroes
when none (tdd SS4.9.1).

SourceRange.description:
The inclusive raw-record range a durable-sourced view event folded from
(tdd SS4.2) — the reconciliation token: re-folding the cited records from
the canonical fold state immediately before `first` — appended host-death
terminals seed from the end-of-records state — reproduces the event
(tdd SS7.5; spec 14653 T041/INV-009). In v1 it is an **opaque provenance
token**: no wire method reads what it points at (the SS6 raw-log altitude
is deferred, #13929).

Ephemeral-sourced events (`item/delta`, and an `item/started` that opens
on an ephemeral record) carry no `sourceRange` — ephemeral records may be
evicted by retention (tdd SS4.2; spec 14653 INV-009).

first.description: The first record of the inclusive range.

last.description:
The last record of the inclusive range; equal to `first` for an event
folded from one record.

stream.description:
The stream the folded records live on (run stream, or the session
stream's mirror of task/approval/subagent-control records — whichever
the fold actually consumed, tdd SS4.2).

StreamRef.description: One raw stream named by a [`SourceRange`] (tdd SS4.2).

kind.description:
The stream kind, verbatim raw-log vocabulary (e.g. `"run"`,
`"session"`). A free string, not an enum: `sourceRange` is an opaque
provenance token in v1 and the raw stream vocabulary is the deferred
SS6 altitude's to freeze (#13929).

SubagentControlStatus.description:
Subagent control status (tdd SS4.5.7, camelCased
`SubagentControlStatus`). Open; the generic item `status` is the terminal
authority.

SubagentInputParams.description:
Params for `subagent/sendMessage` and `subagent/followupTask` (SS3.16):
a child target plus the input body.

body.description:
The note/task text: trimmed with Unicode-whitespace semantics,
rejected when empty after trimming, delivered trimmed with multibyte
content byte-for-byte intact (SS3.16).

subagentId.description: Durable child id (the SS4.5.7 item's `subagentId`; opaque string).

SubagentOwnerReasonParams.description:
Params for `subagent/interrupt`, `subagent/stop`, and `subagent/close`
(SS3.16): a child target plus an optional human-readable reason that is
preserved on the durable effect record.

reason.description: Optional reason, preserved on the durable owner-command record.

subagentId.description: Durable child id (the SS4.5.7 item's `subagentId`; opaque string).

errorKind.description: Error kind, verbatim durable vocabulary, when the child failed.

structuredData.description: Structured result data, verbatim, when present.

SubagentTargetParams.description:
Params for `subagent/resume`, `subagent/reopen`, and
`subagent/readResult` (SS3.16): the bare child target.

subagentId.description: Durable child id (the SS4.5.7 item's `subagentId`; opaque string).

result.description:
Always a JSON object, possibly `{}`, never a bare scalar — so every
result can grow additive-optional members (SS1.2).

activeForm.description: Present-tense active form, when the tool supplied one.

TodoListState.description: The latest todo-list fact in the snapshot (tdd SS4.6.3, SS4.9.1).

revision.description: The snapshot revision. Diagnostics only, never an ordering guard.

sourceTool.description: The tool that produced the snapshot, verbatim.

TodoStatus.description: Todo status (tdd SS4.6.3): closed in the runtime, wire-open.

TokenUsage.description:
Raw token counters, verbatim from the durable record (tdd SS4.6.5, the
runtime's `Usage`, camelCased). Not directly summable across providers —
sum the counted-once derivations instead (#8803).

cacheReadTokens.description: Cache read tokens, only when the provider distinguishes writes/reads.

cacheWriteTokens.description:
Cache write tokens, only when the provider distinguishes
writes/reads.

cachedTokens.description:
Provider-reported cache tokens (inside or beside `inputTokens`,
provider-convention-dependent — the reason `promptTokens` exists).

reasoningTokens.description: Output tokens spent on reasoning, when the provider reports it.

TraceContext.description:
Optional W3C trace context, on requests in both directions only — never on
responses or notifications (SS1.8).

traceparent.description: W3C `traceparent` string; receivers that do not trace ignore it.

TurnCancelParams.description:
`turn/cancel` params (tdd SS3.5): plain cancellation on the normal command
lane. Same shape as `turn/interrupt`, **without** `retract` — pairing a
retract with a plain cancel is durably rejected `not_paired_interrupt`.

turnId.description: The exact turn to cancel; omit to target the current foreground turn.

TurnCompletedParams.description:
`turn/completed` params (tdd SS4.5.1): the run's durable terminal record
landed.

durationMs.description: Turn duration; absent means unmeasured, never fabricated.

error.description:
Present iff `terminal` is `"failed"` (tdd SS4.5.1): mid-turn failures
reach the client here — never as a JSON-RPC error.

reason.description:
The runtime's free-text terminal reason, verbatim. Display and
diagnostics only; never branch on it.

sourceRange.description: The durable records this event folded from.

timeToFirstTokenMs.description: Time to first token, when measured.

usage.description:
The turn's aggregate token usage, summed across the turn's model
completions (same shape as `session/tokenUsage.usage`).

viewCursor.description: Opaque, strictly monotonic view cursor (tdd SS4.1).

TurnError.description:
The settled turn-failure object (tdd SS4.5.1): `{kind, message,
retryable}`.

kind.description:
The failure class (open camelCase enum grounded in the runtime's
terminal failure classification).

retryable.description: The server's judgment that resubmitting the same input may succeed.

TurnErrorKind.description:
Turn failure classes (tdd SS4.5.1, `TerminalErrorKind` plus the
model-task failure class). Open.

TurnInputPart.description:
One ordered content part of a turn submission (tdd SS3.2). File mentions
are text, not a part type: write `@relative/path` in a text part. A
structured `mention` part is reserved and currently rejected, and an
unknown part type is `invalidParams` (tdd SS3.1.2, SS3.2) — which is what
closes [`TurnInputPartType`].

Modelled as a discriminated flat object rather than a Rust `enum`, the
convention [`crate::view::approval::ApprovalSubject`] already established
for a wire union in this crate: the v1 schema model names no
object-variant union shape and fails closed on one. The serialized JSON is
the tdd shape either way; what a flat object cannot express is
"`mediaType` is required exactly when `type` is `image`".

**RULED (#22785 E4, owner, 2026-08-26): the precedent is accepted.** A
strict union node kind may be funded later as a follow-up; if it is, it
must cover [`crate::method::lifecycle::PendingRequestPointer`] too.

base64Data.description:
Base64 payload, required on an `image` part. Invalid base64 or an
empty payload is rejected with invalid params.

height.description:
Pixel height; must be provided together with `width` or not at all
(tdd SS3.2, #22785 E6c).

mediaType.description: Media type, required on an `image` part.

text.description:
User prompt text, on a `text` part. Multiple text parts are joined in
order into the turn's prompt.

width.description:
Pixel width; must be provided together with `height` or not at all
(tdd SS3.2). Published as a `dependentRequired` pair under #22785 E6c.

TurnInputPartType.description:
The `type` discriminator of a turn input part (tdd SS3.2). Closed: an
unknown part type is `invalidParams` (tdd SS3.1.2).

TurnInterruptParams.description:
`turn/interrupt` params (tdd SS3.4): the "user pressed stop" gesture, on
the runtime's priority lane.

retract.description:
Pair a retract intent with the interrupt: if the turn is cancelled
before any assistant output committed, the submission is durably
retracted (view event `turn/retracted`) so the client may restore the
prompt text. A rejected retract does not undo the interrupt. Default
`false` (tdd SS3.4).

turnId.description:
The exact turn to interrupt. Omit to target the session's current
foreground turn, resolved at admission; prefer passing the explicit id
when you have one (tdd SS3.4).

TurnInterruptResult.description:
`turn/interrupt` result (tdd SS3.4). Acceptance means the interrupt was
admitted, **not** that the turn is already stopped: the turn is over when
you fold its `turn/completed` with terminal `cancelled`.

TurnRef.description: A turn named by the snapshot's active/queued lists (tdd SS4.9.1).

commandId.description: The `commandId` of the submit that minted it.

turnId.description: The turn's id, pre-minted per tdd SS3.1.4.

TurnRetractedParams.description:
`turn/retracted` params (tdd SS4.5.1): an interrupt-paired retract was
durably accepted. The retracted user-message item is re-emitted via
`item/updated` with `retracted: true`.

sourceRange.description: The durable records this event folded from.

turnId.description: The turn whose submission was retracted.

viewCursor.description: Opaque, strictly monotonic view cursor (tdd SS4.1).

TurnRetryScheduledParams.description:
`turn/retryScheduled` params (tdd SS4.5.1, spec 14412; D-026): a durable
turn retry-scheduled fact folded — the failing model attempt's scheduled
retry is observable BEFORE the turn terminates, so a streaming client can
render "attempt N/M · retrying in Ss · reason" instead of dead air.
Non-terminal: it never resolves a turn-wait (tdd SS3.1.4). The delay is
the recorded scheduled backoff, never an absolute fire time — clients
derive any countdown locally. `sourceRange` cites the session stream's
mirror of the task-lifecycle record (tdd SS4.2).

nextAttempt.description:
The attempt about to run (producer contract: attempt < nextAttempt
<= maxAttempts; not a schema constraint).

reason.description:
The recorded stopping reason through the shared task-detail
normalization (non-empty; capped at 160 characters).

retryDelayMs.description:
The scheduled backoff delay in milliseconds, verbatim from the
durable fact.

sourceRange.description:
The durable record this event folded from (the session stream's
mirror of the retry-scheduled task status; `first == last`).

turnId.description: The running turn whose model attempt is being retried.

viewCursor.description: Opaque, strictly monotonic view cursor (tdd SS4.1).

TurnStartDisposition.description:
What `turn/start` did with the input (tdd SS3.2). Resolves OQ-H in v1:
since `queue` is the default `ifBusy`, clients need to distinguish these
without folding history.

TurnStartParams.description:
`turn/start.providerRequestOptions` is deliberately absent: **RULED
(#22785 E3, owner, 2026-08-26) to stay off the published schema.** The
schema is the contract, and a free-form-object node kind is revisited only
if the experimental field graduates.
`turn/start` params (tdd SS3.2).

commandId.description:
The SS3.1.1 idempotency handle (UUIDv7). The fresh turn's `turnId`
derives from it (tdd SS3.1.4).

displayText.description:
Presentation form of the prompt for transcripts. Durable; carried on
the resulting user-message view item. Never model-visible (tdd SS3.2).

ifBusy.description: Disposition when a turn is already running; default `queue`.

input.description: Ordered content parts; required and non-empty.

reasoningEffort.description: Reasoning tier sampled at submission for this turn.

startedNewTurn.description:
`true` iff `disposition` is `started`; retained as the boolean
shorthand — `disposition` is authoritative (tdd SS3.2).

turnId.description:
The turn that will carry (or absorbed) this input. Authoritative:
always take it from the ack rather than deriving it (tdd SS3.2).

TurnStartedParams.description:
`turn/started` params (tdd SS4.5.1): a foreground turn began running —
fresh submits immediately, queued submits at their launch boundary, never
steered submits.

commandId.description:
The submitting command; `turnId == commandId` for fresh turns (tdd
SS3.1.4).

sourceRange.description: The durable records this event folded from.

viewCursor.description: Opaque, strictly monotonic view cursor (tdd SS4.1).

TurnSteerParams.description:
`turn/steer` params (tdd SS3.3): exact-target steering into the currently
running turn.

expectedTurnId.description:
The turn you believe is running. Closes the race where the turn
completes or is replaced between your read and your steer: input meant
for turn A can never leak into turn B (tdd SS3.3).

reasoningEffort.description:
Reasoning tier for the model calls this steer's input reaches. Applies
forward, never backward; absent means unspecified, not "reset"
(tdd SS3.3, D-024).

turnId.description: The running turn that absorbed the input.

TurnTerminal.description:
Turn terminal vocabulary (tdd SS4.5.1): exactly the runtime's
`RunTerminalKind` — closed in the runtime, wire-open for evolution.

TurnUnqueueParams.description:
`turn/unqueue` params (tdd SS3.6): reclaim a queued submit before it
launches. It is **not** a stop — a reclaim that arrives after its target
launched is durably rejected, never silently upgraded into a cancel.

turnId.description:
The queued turn to reclaim, exactly as the queueing `turn/start`'s ack
minted it and as snapshot `queuedTurns` lists it. Required, and never
"whichever is newest" (tdd SS3.6).

TurnUnqueueResult.description:
`turn/unqueue` result (tdd SS3.6). Admission only — but for this command
admission *is* the race: an admitted reclaim implies the turn will not
launch. The authoritative removal is the `turn/unqueued` view event.

TurnUnqueuedParams.description:
`turn/unqueued` params (tdd SS3.6, SS4.5.1): a queued submit's reclaim
durably won; its pre-minted turn never runs. Carries the reclaimed
`turnId` and the `commandId` of the `turn/start` that queued it, so a
client can restore the submission's text exactly as for
`turn/retracted`. No `turn/started`/`turn/completed` is ever emitted for
this `turnId` (SDK turn-waits settle on this event too, tdd SS3.1.4).
`sourceRange` cites the SESSION stream's reclaim record — a reclaimed
turn never had a run stream.

commandId.description: The `commandId` of the `turn/start` that queued the reclaimed turn.

sourceRange.description:
The durable records this event folded from (the session stream's
reclaim record).

turnId.description: The reclaimed turn: pre-minted at admission, never launched.

viewCursor.description: Opaque, strictly monotonic view cursor (tdd SS4.1).

UnframedViewNotification.description:
One element of a `view/page` result's `events` array: an **unframed view
notification** exactly as tdd SS4.2.1 defines it — the nested pair
`{"method", "params"}`, which is the live notification minus `jsonrpc`
and `emittedAtMs`, with nothing lifted out of `params` and nothing spliced
into it. SS4.2.1 is the single normative definition; SS4.7.3 and SS7.4
both cite it, so the two surfaces cannot drift.

method.description:
The event type — the live notification's method name, retained because
the type lives only in the notification name and would otherwise be
lost (tdd SS4.2.1).

UnframedViewNotificationParams.description:
The `params` of an unframed view notification (tdd SS4.2.1, SS4.2).

Declares the SS4.2 base members every view notification carries, and stays
**open** for the event-specific fields SS4.5/SS4.6/SS5 add per event type.
The v1 schema model names no method-correlated union (the SS4.7.3 `events`
element's `params` arm is selected by its sibling `method`), so the
per-event arms cannot be expressed here without one; enumerating them as
an uncorrelated union would additionally exclude `turn/unqueued`, whose
notification row is another lane's ratified deferral (#207/#14407) — a
published schema that rejects a real page element is the exact #19923
defect this PR exists to close. Recorded as a Design delta on #22785.

`sourceRange` is required here and not optional: `view/page` serves
durable-sourced events only (tdd SS4.7.3), and durable-sourced is *defined*
as carrying a `sourceRange` — the SS4.2 ephemeral-sourced exemption applies
to `item/delta`, which `view/page` never replays.

sourceRange.description: The durable records this event folded from (tdd SS4.2, SS6.8).

viewCursor.description:
The event's opaque, strictly monotonic view cursor. It stays **inside**
`params`, where every live notification already carries it (tdd
SS4.2.1) — nothing is spliced beside `method`.

UserInputAnswerParams.description:
`userInput/answer` params (tdd SS5.10.2): answer every question.

Each answer carries `questionId` then exactly one of `selectedLabel`
(single mode), `selectedLabels` (multiple mode, within min/max bounds), or
`freeText` (<=500 chars); plus an optional `note` (<=500). Answers that do
not match the prompt fail -32057 `userInputAnswerInvalid`. Image
`attachments` are a **reserved** field in v1, rejected if sent, because
the blob-upload path they reference is reserved in tdd SS3.2.

UserInputCancelParams.description:
`userInput/cancel` params (tdd SS5.10.2): decline to answer; the tool call
resolves with a cancelled result the model sees.

UserInputClarifyParams.description:
`userInput/clarify` params (tdd SS5.10.2): answer with a free-form
clarification instead of the structured options — the "let me explain"
path; the model receives the clarification text and re-decides.

UserInputSettledParams.description: `userInput/settled` params: the first durable prompt settlement.

UserInputSettlementSummary.description: Winning terminal returned to a late user-input command.

Vcs.description: Version-control system of a branch observation (tdd SS4.6.4). Open.

ViewGapParams.description:
`view/gap` params (spec 208 SS4.8, FM-001): push delivery dropped events,
and this names the hole.

The bracket is deferred (D-16487-2): it flushes at the subscription's next
ACCEPTED delivery, never at enqueue time, so `next` always names an event
whose own delivery is proven. A run of consecutive undelivered events
coalesces into one bracket keeping the FIRST range's `after` (D-16487-1).
The gap rides the protected reserved queue, so no wire-interleaving order
against neighbouring deliveries is promised — the cursors carry the
semantics (INV-002, D-16487-3).

On receipt a client may take either sanctioned recovery (D-030, FR-013):
splice-fill — buffer live events at cursors >= `next`, page `(after,
next)` forward, discard the overlap, splice — or re-anchor through the
anchored read surface. The server requires neither, cannot distinguish
clients by their choice, and holds no partial-fill state.

after.description:
The last cursor delivered before the hole — the exclusive lower bound
of the undelivered range. An **opaque** view cursor: clients relay it,
never parse it (tdd SS4.1).

next.description:
The first cursor delivered after the hole — the exclusive upper bound
of the undelivered range, and the position delivery continues from. An
**opaque** view cursor: clients relay it, never parse it (tdd SS4.1).

sessionId.description: The session whose subscription dropped events.

ViewPageAnchor.description:
The `view/page` request-mode anchor (tdd SS4.7.3). Declared **open**: the
tdd spells it "open string enum, v1 value `latestCompaction`".

ViewPageDirection.description:
The `view/page` paging direction (tdd SS4.7.3). Closed: the tdd spells
exactly two values and a third would change the paging contract.

ViewPageParams.description: `view/page` params (tdd SS4.7.3): cursor-paged reads of the session view.

anchor.description:
The cold-client request mode (D-029; spec 208 FR-008), resolved at
call time to the latest installed compaction boundary. The one named
exception to the SS4.1 observed-only rule.

cursor.description:
The exclusive anchor. Forward: the page starts strictly after it;
omitted means from the beginning of the view. Backward: the page ends
strictly before it; omitted means from the head. Mutually exclusive
with `anchor` (tdd SS4.7.3; spec 208 FR-008a).

limit.description:
Maximum events to return, 1–1000. The server MAY return fewer
(tdd SS4.7.3's short-serve rule).

The 1–1000 range is ratified and now **published**: #22785 E6c is
owner-ruled, so the model carries the bound and the bundle renders
`minimum`/`maximum` instead of a bare `integer`.

ViewPageResolvedAnchor.description:
The `resolvedAnchor` echo (tdd SS4.7.3): subsequent pages pass ordinary
cursors, so the anchor never needs re-resolving.

boundaryCursor.description: The view cursor of the resolved boundary's `compaction` event.

events.description:
The page's events, always ascending by `viewCursor` in both
directions. Durable-sourced only; pages are contiguous and can never
skip a cursor.

nextCursor.description:
The anchor for the next page in the same direction: forward, the last
event's cursor; backward, the first's. `null` at the end of the view
in that direction — never omitted.

resolvedAnchor.description:
The resolution echo, present exactly when the request used `anchor`
(tdd SS4.7.3; spec 208 FR-008).

schemaVersion.description:
Snapshot schema version. A client whose generated types are older than
this must fall back to inline/paged history (tdd SS4.9.2, SS2.5.2).

state.description: The complete folded view at `viewCursor` (tdd SS4.9.1).

viewCursor.description:
The cursor the state is folded at; every event after it streams as the
suffix (tdd SS4.9).

ViewUnsubscribeParams.description:
`view/unsubscribe` params (tdd SS4.7.2): remove this connection from the
session's view subscription set — the protocol's single unsubscribe
operation, at the altitude that owns subscriptions (tdd SS2.5.6 points
here). It does not unload the session; unloading is the idle policy
(tdd SS2.8).

ViewUnsubscribeResult.description:
`view/unsubscribe` result (tdd SS4.7.2): the empty object. Idempotent —
unsubscribing while not subscribed returns `{}`.

WorkflowChild.description:
One workflow child's folded state (tdd SS4.5.8,
`WorkflowChildLifecycleFact`), keyed by `(childId, attempt)`.

childId.description: The child's id within the run.

durationMs.description: The child's observed duration, when recorded.

label.description: The child's display label, when recorded.

resultRef.description:
The child's recorded result reference, verbatim, when present — an
opaque string, matching the durable owner.

terminal.description: The child's terminal, turn vocabulary (tdd SS4.5.8).

usage.description: The child's observed usage, when recorded.

approval/decide.description: Decides a pending approval, guarded by the current requirement id against the multi-stage race (SS5.4).

model/list.description: Reads the catalog of models the host will accept in `session/setModel`; a query, not a command (SS3.10).

session/compact.description: Compacts the session's conversation context; runs asynchronously, so the ack is admission only (SS3.7).

session/fork.description: Branches a session into a new id whose log copies the source through a cut point, with durable provenance (SS2.5.3).

session/list.description: Pages through stored sessions under the sessions root for history and picker UIs; read-only, never touches leases (SS2.5.4).

session/read.description: Reads one stored session without attaching: no lease, no load, no subscription, no resume record (SS2.5.5).

session/resume.description: Loads a stored session on this host, auto-subscribes this connection, and returns the history needed to render it (SS2.5.2).

session/setApprovalMode.description: Selects a preconfigured approval enforcement mode mid-session; select, never create (SS5.12).

session/setModel.description: Reconfigures the session's model; the selection is durable and applies to subsequent model calls (SS3.8).

session/start.description: Creates a brand-new session, loads it on this host, durably records the start, and auto-subscribes this connection (SS2.5.1).

session/userShell.description: Runs a user-initiated shell command in the session's workspace; capability-gated on `userShell` (SS3.9).

subagent/close.description: Owner-close a child; the terminal mapping folds per SS4.5.7 (SS3.16).

subagent/followupTask.description: Queue a follow-up task for a child; admission-only ack, the task settles on the child session's view stream (SS3.16).

subagent/interrupt.description: Ask a child to yield at its next boundary; outcome folds to the parent's subagent item (SS3.16, SS4.5.7).

subagent/readResult.description: Consume a ready child result (state-changing; the content is already the subagent item's result field) (SS3.16).

subagent/reopen.description: Reopen a stopped/closed child as a durable later attempt (SS3.16).

subagent/resume.description: Resume a paused/recoverable child as a durable later attempt (SS3.16).

subagent/sendMessage.description: Queue a user note into a running child; admission-only ack, the note settles on the child session's view stream (SS3.16).

subagent/stop.description: Stop a running child; outcome folds to the parent's subagent item (SS3.16, SS4.5.7).

turn/cancel.description: Cancels a turn on the normal command lane, recording no priority interrupt intent (SS3.5).

turn/interrupt.description: Stops the running turn on the runtime's priority lane, optionally pairing a durable retract intent (SS3.4).

turn/start.description: Submits user input to a session; the optional disposition controls queue, steer, or replace when a turn is already running (SS3.2).

turn/steer.description: Injects input into the turn the caller names, failing if that turn is no longer active (SS3.3).

turn/unqueue.description: Reclaims a queued submit before it launches; never upgrades into a cancel once the target is running (SS3.6).

userInput/answer.description: Answers every question of an open user-input prompt (SS5.10.2).

userInput/cancel.description: Declines an open user-input prompt; the tool call resolves with a cancelled result the model sees (SS5.10.2).

userInput/clarify.description: Answers an open user-input prompt with a free-form clarification the model re-decides against (SS5.10.2).

view/page.description: Cursor-paged reads of the session view, forward or backward; each result element is an unframed view notification, the nested {method, params} pair of SS4.2.1 (SS4.7.3).

item/started.description: An item opened on the transcript (SS4.3).

item/updated.description: An open item changed non-terminally: full re-emission at a higher revision (SS4.4.2).

session/approvalModeChanged.description: The approval enforcement mode changed: the fold of the durable reconfigure audit fact (SS5.12).

session/branchChanged.description: A durable workspace-branch observation landed; null branch is a detached-HEAD fact (SS4.6.4).

session/contextUsage.description: A provider-reported context-occupancy fact folded to a changed (windowTokens, usedTokens, pressure) triple (SS4.6.6).

session/goalChanged.description: The session's goal block changed value; replace wholesale, an explicit null clears (SS4.6.2).

session/modelChanged.description: A durable model selection took effect (SS4.6.1).

session/todoListChanged.description: The todo list was replaced wholesale; empty items is a cleared list (SS4.6.3).

session/tokenUsage.description: A model call completed with usage: raw counters plus counted-once derivations plus session cumulative (SS4.6.5).

turn/completed.description: Turn terminal: completed | failed | cancelled, with usage and the settled error object (SS4.5.1).

turn/retracted.description: An interrupt-paired retract was durably accepted (SS4.5.1).
